segments.narration: Wounded Civil War soldiers suddenly began glowing in the dark. In 1862, after the Battle of Shiloh, injured troops lay stranded for days in freezing mud.
As night fell, a faint blue-green light radiated from their skin. Incredibly, the glowing men healed faster and survived at twice the rate of others.
How could a mysterious night glow cure lethal battlefield infections? For over a century, baffled doctors simply called it Angel’s Glow.
The answer came in 2001 from a high school science fair project. Freezing mud gave soldiers hypothermia, allowing a glowing soil bacteria named Photorhabdus luminescens to thrive.
The luminescent bacteria pumped out natural antibiotics, killing deadly pathogens before the men even reached a hospital. A glowing microbe had saved them.
